items.title: NASA highlights starshade concept for imaging Earth-like exoplanets

featured_image.name: Ground-based observatories could use starshades to see planets

items.description: NASA is pushing forward on multiple fronts in its quest to directly photograph planets orbiting distant stars, with a wave of new missions, research breakthroughs, and industry partnerships coming together in early 2026 to lay the groundwork for finding another Earth.

items.title: Oil tops $100 again as Iran strikes Israel, Gulf states

featured_image.name: Stock market news for March 3, 2026 - CNBC

items.description: A fresh barrage of Iranian missiles targeting Israel and Gulf Arab states on Tuesday sent oil prices climbing again, boosting Canada's energy-heavy stock market while dragging Wall Street lower as investors grappled with the four-week-old conflict's toll on the global economy.

items.title: EU delays proposal to permanently ban Russian oil imports

featured_image.name: E.U. Forms Plan to Ban Russian Oil

items.description:
The European Commission will no longer submit a legal proposal to permanently ban Russian oil imports on April 15 as previously planned, an updated EU legislative agenda showed on Tuesday, as the war in Iran sends global crude prices to their highest levels in years.[1][2]

An EU official told Reuters the proposal had not been cancelled and would still be published, though no longer by the mid-April date due to "current geopolitical developments."[2]

items.title: Modi warns of 'serious consequences' as Hormuz crisis deepens

featured_image.name: 'Serious Consequences Imminent...': PM Modi Says 'Aim Is Hormuz Opening And  De-Escalation Of West Asia Tensions'

items.description:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump spoke by phone on Tuesday, with both leaders stressing the need to keep the Strait of Hormuz open as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran continues to disrupt global energy supplies and rattle economies worldwide.

Trump initiated the call, according to U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor, who said on X that the two leaders "discussed the ongoing situation in the Middle East, including the importance of keeping the Strait of Hormuz open". Modi, in his own post on X, said he had a "useful exchange of views" and reiterated India's position. "India supports de-escalation and restoration of peace at the earliest. Ensuring that the Strait of Hormuz remains open, secure and accessible is essential for the whole world," Modi wrote.[1][2][3]

items.title: Altman exits Helion board as OpenAI eyes massive fusion deal

featured_image.name: OpenAI Eyes Fusion Energy Deal With Helion for Future Power Supply | AI  News Hub

items.description:
OpenAI is negotiating a massive power purchase agreement with fusion startup Helion Energy that could deliver 5 gigawatts of electricity by 2030 and scale to 50 gigawatts by 2035, according to a report by Axios on Monday citing a person familiar with the talks. Sam Altman, OpenAI's CEO and Helion's largest individual investor, has stepped down from Helion's board of directors to avoid conflicts of interest as the two companies move toward a partnership.[1][2][3][4]

The proposed deal would give OpenAI a guaranteed 12.5% share of Helion's projected energy output, dwarfing every existing commercial fusion agreement. For context, Helion's only signed power contracts to date are a 50-megawatt deal with Microsoft struck in 2023 and a 500-megawatt plant being developed with steelmaker Nucor — making the OpenAI framework 100 to 1,000 times larger than anything the company has committed to before.[5][3][1]

items.title: 20-year study finds mammal cloning hits genetic dead end after 58 generations

featured_image.name: Starting with one mouse, scientists create 581 successive clones

items.description:
A 20-year experiment in Japan has revealed that mammals cannot be cloned indefinitely, with researchers producing 58 generations of mice from a single donor before the cloned animals accumulated so many genetic mutations they could not survive past their first day of life.

The study, published Tuesday in Nature Communications, was led by geneticist Sayaka Wakayama and developmental biologist Teruhiko Wakayama at the University of Yamanashi. Beginning in 2005, the team used somatic cell nuclear transfer — the same technique that produced Dolly the sheep — to serially clone a single female mouse, producing more than 1,200 offspring across nearly six decades of clonal generations.[1][2]

items.title: OpenAI Foundation pledges $1B in grants for AI safety and health research

featured_image.name: OpenAI Nonprofit Names Leaders, Aims to Spend $1 Billion in 2026

items.description: The OpenAI Foundation, the nonprofit arm that controls the artificial intelligence company behind ChatGPT, announced Tuesday that it plans to grant $1 billion over the next year to fund AI safety, health research, and efforts to mitigate the technology's societal risks. The pledge marks a dramatic escalation in the organization's philanthropic activity, coming just months after OpenAI restructured into a conventional for-profit business.[1][2]

items.title: Saudi crown prince urges Trump to escalate Iran war, deploy ground troops

featured_image.name: Saudi Crown Prince pushes Trump to continue Iran war until regime change as  US eyes exit: Report - The Statesman

items.description:
Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has been pressing President Donald Trump in a series of private conversations to continue and even escalate the war against Iran, arguing that the U.S.-Israeli military campaign presents a "historic opportunity" to reshape the Middle East by toppling the government in Tehran, according to a New York Times report citing people briefed by U.S. officials on the conversations.[1][2]

The revelation comes as the conflict enters its fourth week and Trump has sent mixed signals about its direction, at one point saying he was considering "winding down" military operations.[3][4]

items.title: Stocks slide as Iran strikes dash hopes for quick end to war

featured_image.name: Oil prices rise and stocks fall as war with Iran advances despite Trump's  talk of negotiations | Pittsburgh Post-Gazette

items.description: Oil prices climbed and U.S. stocks slid on Tuesday as Iranian missile strikes across the Middle East undercut hopes for a swift end to the nearly four-week-old conflict between Iran and the U.S.-Israeli coalition. The renewed attacks came just a day after President Trump claimed progress in negotiations with Tehran — assertions Iran flatly denied.

items.title: Iran fears ceasefire talks are a trap to kill its remaining leaders

featured_image.name: Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf leading talks with US

items.description:
Iranian officials believe that U.S. efforts to broker a ceasefire may be a ploy to expose the country's surviving senior leadership to assassination, according to The Wall Street Journal. Tehran is particularly concerned that face-to-face negotiations could be used as a pretext to target Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the speaker of Iran's parliament and a former paramilitary commander, whom Washington has sought to bring to the table.[1][2]

Ghalibaf has so far managed to avoid the Israeli strikes that have killed a succession of top Iranian figures, making him one of the few high-ranking officials still alive. The fears were relayed by Iranian officials to Arab counterparts, the Journal reported Monday.[1]

items.title: Saudi Arabia, UAE edge toward joining war on Iran

featured_image.name: Saudi Arabia expands US base access, UAE prepares for months ...

items.description:
Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are edging toward direct involvement in the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, with Riyadh opening a key air base to American forces and Abu Dhabi dismantling Iranian institutional presence on its soil, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.[1][2]

The moves mark a turning point for two Gulf monarchies that initially lobbied Washington against military action on Iran but have been drawn deeper into the conflict by weeks of Iranian missile and drone strikes on their territory and energy infrastructure.[3][4]

items.title: NASA visualization shows GUARDIAN spotted tsunami 32 minutes before tide gauges

featured_image.name: GUARDIAN Warns Hawaii Early of Incoming Kamchatka Tsunami

items.description: NASA released a new data visualization this week showing how its experimental GUARDIAN tsunami detection system spotted an incoming wave near Hawaii a full 32 minutes before conventional tide gauges during last summer's massive Kamchatka earthquake, underscoring the technology's potential to give coastal communities precious extra time to evacuate.[1][2]

items.title: NASA cancels lunar orbit station, pivots to $20B moon base

featured_image.name: Nasa targets early March to send humans back around the Moon

items.description:
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman on Tuesday announced the agency will cancel its planned Gateway space station in lunar orbit and instead redirect its components toward building a base on the moon's surface, a $20 billion effort expected to take seven years.[1][2]

"It should not really surprise anyone that we are pausing Gateway in its current form and focusing on infrastructure that supports sustained operations on the lunar surface," Isaacman told attendees at a day-long event at NASA headquarters in Washington.[2]

items.title: Russia launches 16 Rassvet satellites to rival Starlink

featured_image.name: Russia to Launch Starlink Rival Later This Year, Roscosmos ...

items.description: Russian private aerospace company Bureau 1440 launched 16 low-Earth orbit satellites on Monday as part of its Rassvet constellation, a state-backed broadband internet project intended to serve as Moscow's answer to SpaceX's Starlink. The launch from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome marks Russia's first step toward building a domestic satellite internet network, though the effort remains dwarfed by its American competitor.

items.title: Israel to occupy southern Lebanon up to Litani River, defence minister says

featured_image.name: Israel destroys river bridges in southern Lebanon

items.description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz declared on Tuesday that the Israeli military will occupy southern Lebanon up to the Litani River, marking the first time Israel has explicitly stated its intent to seize territory amounting to nearly a tenth of Lebanon.[1][2]

items.title: Astronomers crack two 50-year stellar mysteries in rapid succession

featured_image.name: Supercomputers expose how spinning red giants remix their cores

items.description: Two long-standing puzzles in stellar astrophysics have been cracked in rapid succession, with researchers announcing breakthroughs on both the enigmatic surface chemistry of red giant stars and the origin of unusual X-rays from one of the night sky's most visible stars.

items.title: Study finds Europe's last Neanderthals descended from one small group

featured_image.name: Shocking New Study Reveals the Exact Moment Neanderthals Started to  Disappear

items.description: Europe's last Neanderthals descended from a single small population that survived harsh Ice Age conditions by retreating to a climate refuge in what is now southwestern France, according to a study published this week in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The finding adds to a growing body of genetic evidence showing that severe losses of diversity plagued Neanderthal populations long before their final disappearance roughly 40,000 years ago.

items.title: UN report finds freshwater fish migrations collapsing worldwide

featured_image.name: Migratory freshwater fish decline 76 percent since 1970, new ...

items.description:
Some of the longest and most important animal migrations on Earth are happening beneath the surface of the world's rivers — and many are rapidly collapsing. That is the finding of a major new assessment released on Monday at the UN's Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species (CMS) conference in Campo Grande, Brazil, which identifies hundreds of freshwater fish species in urgent need of international protection.[1][2]

The Global Assessment of Migratory Freshwater Fishes, described as the most comprehensive overview ever assembled of migratory freshwater fish conservation needs, found that populations of migratory freshwater fish have declined by roughly 81 percent since 1970. Nearly all — 97 percent — of the 58 CMS-listed migratory fish species are now threatened with extinction.[2][3][1]

items.title: Foreign investors pull $50B from Asian stocks in record March exodus

featured_image.name: Asia stock rout deepens as markets brace for energy shock ...

items.description: Global financial markets remain gripped by volatility as the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran enters its fourth week, with oil prices climbing back above $100 a barrel and foreign investors fleeing Asian equities at a pace not seen since the 2008 financial crisis. Data from LSEG shows approximately $50 billion in net foreign equity outflows from South Korea, Taiwan, India, and Southeast Asian markets throughout March, positioning 2026 for the largest monthly capital flight from the region in nearly two decades.[1][2]

items.title: Business activity slumps across Europe, India and Asia amid Iran war

featured_image.name: Eurozone factory PMI slips back to contraction | trans.info

items.description: Business activity across the eurozone, India and parts of Asia slowed sharply in March as the war in the Middle East drove energy prices higher and sapped demand, according to flash purchasing managers' index data released Tuesday by S&P Global. The surveys, conducted between March 12 and March 20, offer the first broad snapshot of economic damage since the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28.[1][2]
